title: Pharmacoinformatic discovery of plant-derived BRD4 inhibitors as potential therapeutic agents for leukemia.
authors: Lalu, Anjana C; Joseph, Bristow Ben; Varun, T K; Thaikkad, Amritha; Dcunha, Leona; Raju, Rajesh; Jayanandan, Abhithaj
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物源BRD4抑制剂抗白血病，靶向蛋白-组蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Leukemia is a type of blood cancer that occurs when abnormal white blood cells grow too quickly. This uncontrolled growth begins in the bone marrow, where blood cells are produced. Leukemia remains a major health concern due to its high incidence and difficult prognosis. It is the most common type of cancer in children and ranks among the top 15 most prevalent cancers in adults, as reported by the World Health Organization. Several BRD4 inhibitors have shown promising potential as treatments for leukemia. These molecules function by blocking BRD4's interaction with acetylated histones, specifically targeting key amino acid residue ASN140. By disrupting this binding, they offer a potentially more effective therapeutic approach in combating leukemia. Current cancer treatments, such as chemotherapy and targeted therapies like JQ1, frequently come with side effects and toxicity, which highlights the need for safer alternatives. In our study, we explored plant-derived natural compounds that might offer anticancer benefits while being easier on the body. Using advanced techniques like pharmacophore-based virtual screening and ADMET analysis, we identify potential candidates. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations further revealed strong and stable interactions between BRD4 protein and these compounds. Notably, Calyxins C had the best interaction profile, with a docking score of -12.756 kcal/mol and a binding free energy of -85.32 kcal/mol. For Calyxins A, the binding free energy was -72.53 kcal/mol with a docking score of -10.132 kcal/mol, while for Deoxycalyxin A, it was -73.03 kcal/mol with a docking score of -10.162 kcal/mol. Our research indicates that these natural compounds, Calyxins C, Calyxins A, and Deoxyocalyxin A, exhibit higher stability and favorable interaction profiles, which could be effective and less toxic drug leads for leukemia treatment, paving the way for future experimental validation and clinical studies.
abstract_zh: 白血病是一种血液癌症，当异常白细胞过度快速生长时发生。这种不受控制的生长始于骨髓，即血细胞生成的场所。由于高发病率和难以预测的预后，白血病仍然是一个主要的健康问题。据世界卫生组织报告，它是儿童中最常见的癌症类型，并在成人最常见的癌症中位列前15名。几种BRD4抑制剂已显示出作为白血病治疗药物的巨大潜力。这些分子通过阻断BRD4与乙酰化组蛋白的相互作用，特异性地靶向关键氨基酸残基ASN140。通过破坏这种结合，它们提供了一种可能更有效的治疗策略来对抗白血病。目前的癌症治疗方法，如化疗和靶向治疗（如JQ1），常常伴随副作用和毒性，这凸显了对更安全替代方案的需求。在我们的研究中，我们探索了植物来源的天然化合物，这些化合物可能提供抗癌益处，同时对身体更温和。利用药效团虚拟筛选和ADMET分析等先进技术，我们识别出潜在候选物。分子对接和动力学模拟进一步揭示了BRD4蛋白与这些化合物之间的强且稳定的相互作用。值得注意的是，Calyxins C具有最佳的相互作用特征，对接得分为-12.756 kcal/mol，结合自由能为-85.32 kcal/mol。对于Calyxins A，结合自由能为-72.53 kcal/mol，对接得分为-10.132 kcal/mol，而Deoxycalyxin A的结合自由能为-73.03 kcal/mol，对接得分为-10.162 kcal/mol。我们的研究表明，这些天然化合物Calyxins C、Calyxins A和Deoxycalyxin A表现出更高的稳定性和有利的相互作用特征，可能成为白血病治疗中有效且毒性较低的药物先导物，为未来的实验验证和临床研究铺平道路。
